headline_marked: AWS [[billing glitch]] hits customers with $1.5B+ fees
headline: AWS billing glitch hits customers with $1.5B+ fees
summary: Amazon Web Services' billing error causes customers to see huge, incorrect charges
details: A glitch with Amazon Web Services' billing operation led some customers to believe they owed the company billions of dollars. The error caused customers to see incorrect and inflated charges on their AWS bills.

One affected customer, Bill Radjewski, who runs CollegeFootballData.com, received an email alert from AWS stating he had racked up more than $1.5 billion in usage fees, with his August 1 bill on track to be upwards of $3 billion. Radjewski shared screenshots of his recent monthly AWS invoices, which showed charges of $0.01 each.

The issue, characterized as "global" by AWS, began displaying incorrect estimated billing data on Thursday, July 16 at 10:38 PM ET. The company started investigating about six hours later and concluded that the "root cause" of the error was "an issue with unit pricing within the estimated billing computation subsystem".

AWS said it is rolling back a recent change to the billing computation subsystem and attempting to revert to its "last known good estimated bill computation". The company also paused estimated billing computations and expects the issue to be resolved by this weekend, with no customer actions required.
